problem_type: Passive MCP discovery starts the desktop application
symptom: On Windows, listing MCP resources or reconnecting a client can show the Nomi window; after closing it, the window returns later.
direct_cause: The protocol resources/list handler calls invokeForRequest('skills.list'), and the launcher invoke path always calls ensureLiveInstance, which starts Nomi when no advertisement exists.
class_root: Passive MCP discovery has no probe-only transport boundary; discovery and real work share a cold-starting invocation path.
affected_population: Nomi instances with no live advertisement
entry_points: Electron desktop createWindow and second-instance lifecycle
internal_only_reason: The invariant is an application-owned separation between passive discovery and cold-starting work; no third-party behavior determines it.
invariants: Passive discovery never calls a cold-starting invoke path
Only real tool/work requests may start Nomi
A background window remains hidden until an explicit desktop open action
Idle exit is allowed only before the window has ever been shown and when the existing in-flight task owner reports no active task

door_reduction.why_not: The 28 doors are distinct protocol, launcher, task-cache, passive-discovery, navigation, and desktop lifecycle entry points. They converge on the probe-only transport or background lifecycle boundary but remain separate owners by responsibility; none can be merged without creating a second owner for protocol dispatch, launcher startup, task state, navigation, or window lifecycle.

generality_proof: All discovery methods are handled by the single MCP protocol dispatcher, while all launcher calls pass through the transport. Routing passive resources/list through invokeIfOpen prevents cold start for every client and library state; real tool calls retain ensureLiveInstance.

shared_boundaries.responsibility: Classify passive discovery and use probe-only invocation when an instance is already live.
Read the live advertisement and call RPC without spawning Nomi.
Own the pre-display background idle timer and require both elapsed idle and no in-flight work before exit.

same_class_entry_points.evidence: This is the reported passive handler that previously called cold-starting invokeForRequest.

Neither calls transport invocation; tests lock the passive set.

recurrence.reason: Any MCP client can issue discovery repeatedly while Nomi is closed, so the shared invoke path can repeatedly relaunch the GUI.
same_class_scan: rg for createWindow/show/focus/second-instance in main.ts and productionRunDesktopLifecycle.ts

prevention.invariant: Passive discovery uses only an already-live RPC instance; cold start is reachable only from real work invocation.
prevention.failure_mode: If no instance is advertised, passive discovery returns static resources and never spawns; real work keeps the existing explicit startup error/timeout behavior.
prevention.strategy: Separate probe-only invocation from ensureLiveInstance at the transport boundary and route the sole passive dynamic resource lookup through it.

legacy_paths.rationale: No file or entry point was deleted: the passive discovery handlers in mcpProtocol.ts were rerouted in place from the cold-starting invoke to the probe-only invokeIfOpen, and the moved main.ts code lives on in backgroundLaunch.ts and windowNavigation.ts.

dependency_lifecycle.rationale: No third-party dependency controls the lifecycle invariant.

migration: No persisted data changes; existing clients receive static discovery results while Nomi is closed and dynamic skill resources when it is already live.
residual_risks: Windows packaged real-machine walk is required to prove renderer startup and 10-minute process exit; unit tests cover the decision boundary.
